text:
Maya: Quick design check — split preview in the catalog (left: filters, right: compare table) feels super dense at smaller widths. Thinking about collapsing filter groups into a sticky horizontal pill row to free up table width. @Juan @Kevin :eyes:

Juan: I prototyped a collapse that turns groups into chips with an overflow menu. Keeps the compare table wider. GIF in Figma comment (won't paste here).

Kevin: One concern — when you pin a model from the compare table, where does pin state surface in the collapsed filter chips? The mock currently shows nothing on chips, which feels disconnected.

Aria: Accessibility nit: chips need aria-pressed and a visible focus ring. Collapse toggle must have aria-expanded and a descriptive label (e.g., "Collapse filter groups"). Also ensure keyboard users can get to overflow.

Maya: For pin state I was picturing a tiny badge on the chip (star or "P"). But worried this adds noise. Maybe show pin on hover only?

Juan: Hover-only breaks discoverability for non-mouse users. Recommend persistent small icon plus a visually hidden label for screen readers.

Kevin: Related: performance badges (latency / cost) are already competing for horizontal space in the compare rows. Proposal: collapse those into a single "Perf" badge that expands to show metrics.

Maya: I like collapsing them, but tooltip-only expansion must be keyboard accessible. Alternative: inline expand/collapse on the perf badge (chevron) so metrics appear in-row without covering content.

Aria: Inline expansion OK, as long as it doesn't cause focus loss or unexpected reflow. Animate height gently and respect prefers-reduced-motion. Make sure expanded region is reachable by keyboard and announced.

DesignBot: Accessibility checklist suggestion: 1) chips: role=button or button element, aria-pressed present; 2) perf badge: toggleable via Enter/Space and has aria-expanded; 3) focus order preserved when inserting pinned columns; 4) contrast for badges >= 4.5:1.

Juan: Implementation idea: collapsed chip row should be sticky and horizontally scrollable. Pin icons remain inline as 12px SVGs but with 24px tap/click targets. For keyboard we add tabindex=0 and an onKeyDown handler. Example snippet:

Juan: ```html
<button class="chip" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Pin version v1.2">
  v1.2 <svg class="pin"/>
</button>
```

Maya: Two product decisions before dev: 1) Does pinning a version auto-insert a pinned compare column? 2) When filters are collapsed, do pinned badges remain visible on compare rows or only on chips?

Kevin: My vote: pinning should auto-insert a pinned column at the left (index 0) so it's obvious. Pinned badges should mirror in the chip row for quick context.

Aria: If a column is inserted, we should announce via live region: "Version v1.2 pinned to comparison" so screen reader users are aware of the change. Also announce when pins are removed.

Juan: Dev concern: inserting a column can jump scroll positions and break selection. Plan: animate the column insertion and preserve horizontal scroll offset by adjusting scrollLeft during the transition.

Maya: Good call. I'll update the mock to show: persistent pin icon on chips (with sr-only label), single collapsible perf badge with accessible toggle, sticky horizontal chip row, pinned-column insertion animation, and live region announcements. Any objections?

Kevin: No objections. Also small copy tweak: change button text from "Pin" to "Pin version" to reduce ambiguity when used in other contexts.

Aria: +1 on the copy. Also add microcopy for reduced-motion users: "Animations reduced" where applicable or honor the OS setting.

Juan: I'll spike this and post a screenshot + estimation tomorrow. I think this should be a 3-4 dev days task if the compare table layout utilities are reusable.

Maya: Thanks all — I'll push updated Figma frames and tag everyone.

Kevin: :thumbsup:

Aria: Thanks — adding these to the accessibility checklist now.

DesignBot: Heads up: scheduling a follow-up accessibility review for Wednesday 10am PT.

Maya: Noted, will be there.

Juan: I'll upload the prototype by EOD tomorrow.
